sample_unit: cases (still images and video clips) read by 6 in-training endoscopists

links.outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy and AUC with vs without AI assistance on still images and videos
links.effect: Reader accuracy rose from 74.92% to 86.66% (M1, AUC 0.742 to 0.860) and to 86.81% (M2, AUC 0.796 to 0.900), all p<0.05. Stand-alone AI accuracy was 91.31% (M1) and 92.51% (M2).
links.quote: With AI assistance, overall reader accuracy increased from 74.92% to 86.66% in M1 (AUC 0.742 to 0.860) and likewise from 74.92% to 86.81% in M2 (AUC 0.796 to 0.900); all p < 0.05.

screen.reason: The study evaluated an imaging diagnostic AI tool in an offline reader study comparing endoscopists' performance with vs. without AI assistance. While it evaluates clinician-AI collaboration, it evaluates the tool itself rather than a specific deployment practice or operational safeguard.
